name: Question 1
worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{n}∼N(n\mu ,\,n{\sigma }^{2}).
$$

Therefore, since ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{14}$ are independent and identically distributed, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{14} & ∼N(14\cdot 5,\,14\cdot {2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(14\cdot 5,\,14\cdot 4) \\  & =N(70,56).\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to compute the probability $P(70\le Y\le 78).$ We first convert $Y$ into a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(70\le Y\le 78) & =P(\frac{70-70}{\sqrt{56}}\le Z\le \frac{78-70}{\sqrt{56}}) \\  & =P(0\le Z\le \frac{8}{\sqrt{56}}) \\  & =P(0\le Z\le 1.07) \\  & =Φ(1.07)-Φ(0) \\  & =Φ(1.07)-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we have

$$
Φ(1.07)=0.8577.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(70\le Y\le 78)=Φ(1.07)-0.5=0.8577-0.5=0.3577.
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where

Xi∼N(μ,σ2),1≤i≤n,

then

Y=X1+X2+⋯+Xn∼N(nμ,nσ2).

Therefore, since X1,X2,…,X14 are independent and identically distributed, we have

Y=X1+X2+⋯+X14∼N(14⋅5,14⋅22)∼N(14⋅5,14⋅4)=N(70,56).

We wish to compute the probability P(70≤Y≤78). We first convert Y into a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(70≤Y≤78)=P(70−7056≤Z≤78−7056)=P(0≤Z≤856)=P(0≤Z≤1.07)=Φ(1.07)−Φ(0)=Φ(1.07)−0.5

From the z-table, we have

Φ(1.07)=0.8577.

Therefore,

P(70≤Y≤78)=Φ(1.07)−0.5=0.8577−0.5=0.3577.
